content.value_statement: Teams need reliable examples for connecting TypeScript services to Azure PostgreSQL without unsafe query patterns. This skill provides node-postgres setup, authentication options, pooling, transactions, and TypeScript usage guidance.
actual_capabilities: Shows password and Microsoft Entra ID authentication patterns for Azure PostgreSQL.
Defines required environment variables for pg client and pool configuration.
Demonstrates connection pooling, cleanup, timeouts, and pool event handling.
Shows parameterized queries, transactions, and a reusable transaction helper.
Explains token refresh for long-running passwordless applications.
Lists pg TypeScript types and common PostgreSQL error handling cases.
limitations: It does not create Azure PostgreSQL servers or configure Azure resources.
It does not replace application-specific security review or load testing.
It does not provide migrations, schema design, or ORM integration patterns.
Examples require real environment values and validation in the target project.

use_cases.title: Connect a TypeScript API
use_cases.description: Set up pg client or pool configuration for an API that uses Azure PostgreSQL.

use_cases.title: Adopt Passwordless Authentication
use_cases.description: Use Microsoft Entra ID tokens with node-postgres for managed identity deployments.

use_cases.title: Harden Database Access Patterns
use_cases.description: Apply parameterized queries, transactions, timeouts, SSL, and cleanup practices in service code.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help me connect a TypeScript Node.js service to Azure PostgreSQL with pg and password authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Production Pool
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for reusable pooled connections.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a pg connection pool for Azure PostgreSQL with SSL, timeouts, cleanup, and safe query examples.

prompt_templates.title: Convert to Entra ID
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to replace password authentication with Microsoft Entra ID authentication for Azure PostgreSQL in a TypeScript service.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Data Access Layer
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of reliability and security patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my TypeScript PostgreSQL access layer for pooling, token refresh, transactions, parameterized queries, and shutdown handling.

output_examples.input: I need a TypeScript API to connect to Azure PostgreSQL with a password.
output: Recommended environment variables for host, database, user, password, and port.
A pg connection pattern that uses SSL and closes connections reliably.
A reminder to keep credentials outside source control.

output_examples.input: I want passwordless Azure PostgreSQL access from a hosted service.
output: A managed identity approach using Microsoft Entra ID tokens.
Guidance on token refresh before expiry for long-running services.
Connection pool settings that keep SSL enabled for Azure.

output_examples.input: Review my PostgreSQL query style for injection risk.
output: A focus on parameterized query patterns instead of string concatenation.
Transaction guidance for related write operations.
Suggested error handling cases for common PostgreSQL failures.

best_practices: Use connection pools for production services and close them during shutdown.
Use parameterized queries for all user-controlled values.
Keep SSL enabled and refresh Entra ID tokens before expiry.
anti_patterns: Do not concatenate user input into SQL strings.
Do not hardcode real database passwords in source files.
Do not leave clients or pools open after application shutdown.

faq.question: Does this skill support passwordless Azure PostgreSQL connections?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Microsoft Entra ID token examples using DefaultAzureCredential.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on TypeScript application connection code and database access patterns.

faq.question: Which package does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses pg, also known as node-postgres, with TypeScript type support.

faq.question: Does it cover SQL injection prevention?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes parameterized queries and shows safe query patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with production connection pooling?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers pool size, idle timeouts, connection timeouts, events, and cleanup.

faq.question: Does it include ORM guidance?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on direct pg usage rather than Prisma, TypeORM, or Sequelize.
